title: TextureRect oversampling doesn't account for expand and stretch modes
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible on v4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf ### System information Linux Mint 22.3 Zena ### Issue description When using DPITexture with TextureRect for DPI-varying icons, I noticed that the drawn texture oversampling doesn't account for other modes of `TextureRect::stretch_mode` and `TextureRect::expand_mode. For example, when using `icon.svg` which comes with all new godot projects, import as DPITexture and add it to a TextureRect node without changing the stretch mode, I can see that the oversampling feature works as intended, using the appropriate scaled version for the zoom level. But when I change the modes, so I can draw the texture on a smaller rect, for example, I can see on the editor some aliasing, from using a higher scale version of the texture on a smaller draw rect, thus having a higher dpi than expected. I tried to print the screen to show the aliasing, but it's hard to tell on the picture. It's easier instead to see the inverse effect, by using two .svg files, one with the original scale and other with 1/4 of the scale, I expected both having the same dpi on same drawn rect, but you can see that the right texture is blurry: This doesn't happen when I change `CanvasItem::oversampling_with_scale` to `OVERSAMPLING_WITH_SCALE_ENABLED`, revert `expand_mode` and `stretch_mode` to the default values and instead use `offset_transform_scale` and `offset_transform_visual_only`, thus the oversampling scales with the CanvasItem's global transform scale: ### Steps to reproduce 1. Import `icon.svg` as a DPITexture; 2. Add it to a `TextureRect`; 3. Change `expand_mode` to `EXPAND_IGNORE_SIZE` and `stretch_mode` to `STRETCH_KEEP_CENTERED`; 4. Originally, `icon.svg` is 128x128, mess around with the TextureRect's size to other sizes, for example 32x32 to see aliasing on the editor and 512x512 to see the texture blurry. 5. Also zoom in and out to see how both oversampling problems behave on changing zoom levels. ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [dpitexture_oversampling_bug.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31883503/dpitexture_oversampling_bug.zip)
